title: 3 Space Mysteries Nobody Has Solved
topic: The most mysterious discoveries in space
angle: Real, unexplained observations - a signal, a visitor, and the missing 95% of the universe

beats.text: This 72-second signal from space still has no confirmed explanation.
A radio telescope caught it in 1977. The astronomer who spotted it simply wrote: Wow. It has never been detected again.

visual.description: a radio signal waveform rising and fading

extra_shots.description: the word Wow written next to the signal

beats.text: In 2017, an object from another star system shot straight through our solar system.

visual.description: artist's impression of the interstellar object 'Oumuamua

beats.text: Astronomers named it Oumuamua, and it sped up in a way gravity alone could not explain.

visual.description: dust and debris drifting in space

beats.text: Then there are fast radio bursts: flashes lasting a few milliseconds, arriving from distant galaxies. Some of them even repeat.

extra_shots.description: a distant galaxy photographed by Hubble

beats.text: And everything made of normal matter, every star, planet and person, adds up to only about five percent of the universe.
The other ninety-five percent? We still don't know what it is.

visual.description: Hubble deep field full of galaxies

sources.claim: Wow! signal detected by Ohio State's Big Ear radio telescope on 15 Aug 1977; Jerry Ehman wrote 'Wow!' on the printout; 72-second observation window; never detected again
sources.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wow!_signal ; Big Ear Radio Observatory archive (bigear.org)

sources.claim: 'Oumuamua (1I/2017 U1) discovered Oct 2017, first known interstellar object; showed non-gravitational acceleration
Fast radio bursts last milliseconds, mostly originate in other galaxies, some repeat
Normal (baryonic) matter is about 5% of the universe; the rest is dark matter (~27%) and dark energy (~68%) whose nature is unknown
